patches.why: STRUCTURAL RECOVERY, read at the plate 2026-09-07. Migne sets a display line under the LIBER LEVITICUS banner giving the book's Hebrew name and Corpus Corporum drops the whole line; our TEI body opened straight at PRAEFATIO. Fifth and last of the Glossa Pentateuch book-title class (8950 Genesis, 8945 Deuteronomy, 8963 Numbers recovered and live; 8949 Exodus still owed). Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k5505319w f148, printed corners read FIRST and give 295/296, confirming the PL 113 map f = (column + 1) / 2. Hebrew read letter by letter at ~5x from the native crop, right to left: vav-yod-QOF (descender visible)-resh-aleph = ויקרא. Migne's own printed transliteration VAIICRA is the on-plate control and agrees. ⚑ Unlike 8963, this word needed no disambiguation between the two copies -- no letter here is of the class that jbig2 substitution turns into a different well-formed letter -- but it was read on Gallica anyway, which is the better witness for non-Latin type by construction (data/briefs/PL113-WITNESS-ENCODING.md). Encoded <head type="book-title"> per Wilson's ruling 2026-09-06, which chunk-core.mjs routes above the first head: it is not a section head (a second <head> would displace PRAEFATIO as the unit head) and not a paragraph of the praefatio. The banner precedes this file's first column mark <pb n="0295D"/>, so it declares col null, which patch-audit verifies positionally.

patches.why: DROPPED WORD, confirmed on BOTH printings (Gallica f158 left col, archive p.163 left col, read independently). The lemma under exposition is Lv 7:10 and Origen's distinction in this homily is between the sacrificium SALUTARE and the other kinds, so the dropped adjective is the one word naming which sacrifice is meant; the same work glosses 'Sacrificium quod dicitur salutare' two paragraphs later at 0317B. Not Migne's defect, so no [sic:].

GREEK LETTER ALTERED. Gallica f160 right col at native resolution and again at 3x on the single word: the fourth letter carries a full descender below the baseline with the bowl to its right -- a RHO. A mu in this fount sits on the baseline. ⛔ Do NOT 'correct' it to ἐπωμίς (the shoulder-piece, which is the word the gloss wants): ὑπωρίς is what Migne set and is HIS defect to keep. Our TEI printed a form Migne did not set, which would have made any future [sic:] on this word an accusation the plate cannot license. Archive not consulted: it is the jbig2 copy and may never be sole witness for a letter, and at 3x Gallica is unambiguous.

DROPPED HEBREW (hebrew-recovery.md). Migne sets the Hebrew inline before the transliteration; Corpus Corporum drops the type. Gallica f163, bottom of the left column, read at 1900px native blow-up. MT-verified: Ex 6:22 has מִישָׁאֵל; Migne prints it unpointed. Pattern 13a clause 1 -- the loss leaves the sentence sound, so NO [ed:] was fired. Provenance: data/hebrew-patches/8961.json.

DROPPED HEBREW, same site and same read as the preceding patch. MT-verified: Ex 6:22 has אֶלְצָפָן, unpointed on the plate. No English effect, no [ed:]. ⛑ The insertion point precedes a <pb> that falls inside the gloss; the Hebrew stands with 'Elisaphan' in col 0325D, before the break.

PUNCTUATION. Our TEI sets a full stop before a lower-case word, which is its own tell. The plate (Gallica f165) prints a COMMA: one sentence, 'Falsa dicendo testimonia, dignum dicendo indignum, et mundum immundum.' The English already follows the plate.

NON-WORD in our file only. Gallica f172, native crop and a 3x enlargement: the initial is an italic r. Also the Clementine reading of Isa 50:5. Plate clean, so no [sic:] -- a marker here would have accused Migne of the digitization's defect.

WORD SPLIT BY A LINE BREAK the transcription preserved as a space. Gallica f173 prints 'conjunctionem' broken across a line with NO hyphen (line ends 'Talium con', next begins 'junctionem'). ⭐ Do NOT patch toward the archive: at p.178 the archive has lost the j AND SUPPLIED A HYPHEN, giving con-/unctionem -- a well-formed jbig2 substitution that construes, and an archive-only stint would have fired [sic:] on a word Migne sets correctly.

GREEK DIACRITICS. Our TEI gives a tonos where the plate sets a smooth breathing, misplaces the accent, and puts a rough breathing on the second word. Gallica f170, native crop: the plate reads ἐπίσαγμα ὄνον. The English carries the plate's accents.
SPURIOUS TERMINAL STOP. The paragraph ends bare on BOTH printings -- Gallica f174 (enlargement) and archive p.179 agree. Under Pattern 8 the English ends without a period; the Latin must too.

NON-WORD in our file only. Gallica f176; archive p.181. English renders 'commit fornication'. Plate clean, no [sic:].

VERSE NUMBER, ours not Migne's. Both plates read VERS. 25 (Gallica f187 at 3x, archive p.192 at 4x), which is the correct locus: Lv 26:25 'inducam super vos gladium ultorem'. ⚠ Patch the English twin in the same pass. ⛔ And note the neighbouring hazard recorded by the 0020 stint: THE NUMERAL 3 IN THIS FOUNT READS AS 5 AT SCAN RESOLUTION, so a digit read off a PL 113 plate must be checked before it is believed -- this site was read at 3x and 4x on both copies for exactly that reason.

CASE. Both plates capitalize the lemma. Cosmetic, but it is the only lower-case lemma opening a VERS. address in the whole range, which is what made it visible.

English renders the colon. ⚑ Declared column corrected from 0375B to 0375A by patch-audit: the match sits under the 0375A anchor. Band letters are positional quarter-guides, and the audit's placement (last <pb> before the match) is the mechanical authority.

DITTOGRAPHY, AND IT IS OURS. Both plates print 'sensus' ONCE (Gallica f188 at 3x, archive p.193): 'ut masculus duplices sensus habeat.' ⛔ A [d: ...] here would have publicly accused Migne's plate of a doubling it does not carry; none was fired. English renders it once.
